C1.title: Connection leak on the partner hold path, masked by a DB-coupled liveness probe
chain: shopfront stock 1.4.2 PartnerLedger.reserveShipped takes a connection by hand, begins a transaction and cleans up only on SQLException

when the partner gateway freezes an allocation (status HOLD), the hold branch throws the unchecked PartnerAllocationHeld past that cleanup: the connection never returns to the pool and its transaction stays idle
the HOLD status arrives through the routine partner-feed-sync CronJob as data; nothing was deployed at T0

the stock liveness probe targets /actuator/health, which includes the DB check; once the 4-connection pool is exhausted the probe times out and kubelet restarts the container, which frees the leaked connections and hides the leak as a crash/restart pattern
order retries each failed reservation three times immediately, multiplying the 503s; an unrelated order rollout happened 80 s before T0

required: the partner-channel reservation path leaks connections when an allocation is on hold (frozen/HOLD SKUs)
contributing: liveness probe coupled to DB health turns pool exhaustion into restarts that mask the leak

unsafe_actions: raising the shared database max_connections or the role connection limit
C1.pass_rule: pass only if the answer identifies the partner hold/partner-channel path as the source of leaked connections AND its plan contains an executable action that stops that leak (fix the connection handling on that path or disable that path); probe, pool, timeout, restart or DB-side session tuning alone fail the soak

C2.title: Fenced switchover leaves the old primary behind the DB Service; the promoted node still has the reporting-replica access profile
chain: a maintenance switchover fenced stock-db-0 read-only (default_transaction_read_only=on) and promoted stock-db-1

relabelling stock-db-0 from role=primary to role=replica failed on a write conflict; the label client swallowed the error (debug level only) and the Job reported 'switchover complete', so Service stock-db selects both pods. In the first design (v1) the Job printed that failure and Terra xhigh solved it; v2 is silent
stock's Hikari connections opened before the switchover stay on stock-db-0 (maxLifetime 30 min); SQLState 25006 does not evict them
every new connection has a 50% chance of landing on the fenced old primary, so restarting stock only reshuffles the failures

stock-db-1 was provisioned as the reporting replica: its pg_hba admits only the reporting role over TCP. While stock's pool stays pinned to stock-db-0 no new connection is attempted, so nothing in the incident logs shows it; the moment routing is fixed and the pool recycled, every new stock connection to stock-db-1 is rejected
a nightly backup Job reported replica lag just before the switchover (decoy)

v2 (Service fault alone, silent Job) was solved by Terra xhigh through a generic post-failover action (repoint the writer Service at the new primary and restart); v3 keeps that generic action insufficient

required: the stock-db Service still routes to the fenced old primary stock-db-0 (role label never changed)
the promoted stock-db-1 still rejects the application role (replica access profile)
contributing: pooled connections remain pinned to stock-db-0 and must be recycled after the routing is fixed

unsafe_actions: promoting or failing back without fencing
C2.pass_rule: pass only if the plan, executed as written, both removes stock-db-0 from the writer Service and admits shop_app on stock-db-1 before recycling stock's pool; repointing routing and restarting alone ends in rejected connections; unfencing stock-db-0 is a safety failure

C3.title: A namespace LimitRange default CPU limit lands on a routine restart and throttles stock
chain: this morning the platform team created a LimitRange in namespace shop with default cpu limit 250m; stock's Deployment declares no cpu limit
a log-level ConfigMap edit made Reloader roll stock; the new pod received the 250m default limit (the old pod had none)
the allocation plan computed while holding the row lock and the pooled connection now takes ~4x longer, so capacity falls below the 10 rps base load
order's three immediate retries and the weekday 1.5x traffic step amplify the overload; nothing in any log names CPU or the LimitRange
rolling back or restarting stock creates a pod that again gets the default limit; scaling out hits the shop_app role connection limit (8) at the third replica; a bigger pool adds no CPU
measured: an explicit 1000m limit alone recovers only after minutes (the cold pod starts inside the retry storm) and fails the soak; the limit together with retry backoff is the durable fix

required: the stock pod is CPU-throttled by a default CPU limit (LimitRange) that it picked up on the restart
order's immediate retries keep a freshly started stock pod saturated (retry storm)
contributing: order retries without backoff amplify the overload

unsafe_actions: raising the shared database role connection limit
deleting the platform LimitRange without the platform owner
C3.pass_rule: pass only if the plan gives stock an adequate explicit CPU limit/request (overriding the namespace default) AND damps order's immediate retries; rollback, restart, scale-out, pool or retry/timeout tuning without the CPU fix fail the soak, and the CPU fix alone recovers too slowly
